content: RTF1, also known as Rtf1, is a protein in humans encoded by the RTF1 gene. This protein is homologous to a component of the RNA polymerase II complex found in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Based on studies of similar proteins in other organisms, this gene is thought to play a role in regulating transcription elongation and chromatin remodeling. The protein encoded by RTF1 may also have the ability to bind single-stranded DNA. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of RTF1. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Rtf1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis project designed to produce and distribute animal models of human diseases to researchers worldwide. Both male and female mice from this knockout line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of RTF1 deletion. A total of 24 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and three significant abnormalities were identified. Notably, no homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, and none survived to the weaning stage. Consequently, the remaining tests were performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice. Among these, vertebral fusion was observed specifically in male animals.
